**chameleon-rs** is a Rust implementation of the
[Chameleon](https://github.com/malthe/chameleon) page template engine for Python. It aims to
be a drop-in replacement: the same template language, the same Python API, byte-identical
output, and much faster rendering.

```python
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate

page = PageTemplate('<p tal:repeat="name names">Hello, ${name}!</p>')
print(page(names=['World', 'Rust']))
```

```html
<p>Hello, World!</p>
<p>Hello, Rust!</p>
```

## Why chameleon-rs

- **Drop-in.** Chameleon's own test suite passes unmodified, and two production Flask/Quart
  sites render byte-identical HTML on every page. An existing app switches with one line at
  startup, and nothing else changes.
- **Fast.** Rendering is about 4x to 7x faster than Chameleon on synthetic pages, and about 2.2x
  faster across real application pages, where the app's own Python code takes most of the
  time. Templates compile about 70x faster, so the first request after a deploy or reload is
  quick too.
- **Partials built in.** Every template can call
  `${render_partial('shared/card.pt', item=item)}`. The partial renders natively inside
  the page, about 10x faster than Chameleon with chameleon_partials.
- **Flask and Quart built in.** `chameleon_rs.flask` has chameleon-flask's API.
- **No runtime dependencies.** The package uses only the standard library. Stock Chameleon
  doesn't need to be installed.

## Install

```bash
uv pip install chameleon-rs
```

chameleon-rs needs Python 3.12 or later. The wheels include the compiled engine, so you don't
need a Rust toolchain.

## Switch an existing app

Put this at the very top of your app's entry point, before anything imports Chameleon:

```python
import chameleon_rs.compat

chameleon_rs.compat.install()
```

From then on, `import chameleon`, `import chameleon_partials` and `import chameleon_flask`
all give you chameleon-rs. See [Switching from Chameleon](user-guide/switching-from-chameleon.qmd).
